title: Agentic AI and Autonomous Finance for Firms
summary: An eight-module programme helping firms deploy AI agents that act and transact with sound authority, controls, governance and customer protection.
intro: This training programme equips regulated firms to deploy and oversee AI agents that act and transact, with clear delegated authority, robust controls and governance that protects customers and stands up to supervisory scrutiny.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To equip firms to understand how AI agents are moving from giving information to taking action, and the new risks this creates for authority, identity, payments, liability and financial crime. Participants leave able to design controls and governance for agentic AI and to see their firm's agent strategy the way a supervisor does.
sections.What It Covers: AI agents and agentic finance, delegated authority and mandates, identity and know your agent, payments by agents, controls and kill-switches, liability and customer outcomes, financial crime, third-party models, and governance and board oversight.
Intended Audience: Product, digital, technology and innovation leads designing or deploying AI agents
Compliance, risk, financial crime and legal professionals overseeing agentic AI
Senior managers and directors accountable for AI strategy and its outcomes
Learning Objectives: Explain how AI agents act and transact and where they are used in financial services
Design delegated authority, mandates and identity controls for agents
Assess payment, liability and customer outcome risks from agent actions
Implement controls, monitoring and kill-switches for agentic systems
Identify financial crime and third-party model risks and adapt controls
Establish governance and board oversight and agree a readiness plan
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with case studies, control design exercises and group discussion, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's agentic use cases.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some familiarity with AI, payments or digital products in a regulated firm is helpful. No technical background in AI is required.
Core Reading: OECD, Recommendation of the Council on Artificial Intelligence (2019, revised 2024)
NIST, Artificial Intelligence Risk Management Framework (AI RMF 1.0) (2023)
FSB, The Financial Stability Implications of Artificial Intelligence (2024)

modules.title: From Generative AI to Agentic Finance
modules.summary: What AI agents are, how they differ from chatbots and traditional automation, and where they are beginning to act and transact in financial services.
objectives: Explain how AI agents plan, use tools and act on behalf of users
Distinguish assistive, delegated and autonomous agent models
Identify current and near-term agentic use cases in the firm's sector
syllabus: Agents, tools, memory and multi-agent systems
From advice to action: agents that execute, trade and pay
The layers of agentic finance: governance, decision, assets and settlement
Use cases across banking, payments, investment and insurance

modules.title: Delegated Authority and Mandates
modules.summary: How a firm defines what an agent is permitted to do, on whose behalf and within what limits, whether the agent is the firm's own or a customer's.
objectives: Define the scope, limits and duration of authority given to an agent
Design mandates and permissions for firm-operated and customer agents
Identify where delegated authority creates legal and conduct uncertainty
syllabus: Principals, agents and mandates: who is acting for whom
Permissions, spending limits, scopes and expiry
Customer consent, revocation and changes of instruction
Agents acting across firms and platforms

modules.title: Identity and Know Your Agent
modules.summary: How firms identify, authenticate and trust AI agents, link them to an accountable person or entity, and adapt customer due diligence to agent-initiated activity.
objectives: Explain the know your agent concept and emerging trust frameworks
Design controls to authenticate agents and bind them to a principal
Adapt onboarding and due diligence for agent-initiated relationships
syllabus: Agent identity, credentials and verifiable attestations
Binding agents to customers, firms and developers
Distinguishing legitimate agents from bots and impersonation
Due diligence implications of agent-initiated onboarding and activity

modules.title: Payments and Transactions by Agents
modules.summary: How agents initiate payments and transactions across traditional and new payment rails, and the authorisation, authentication and dispute issues this raises.
objectives: Explain how agents initiate payments across card, account and tokenised rails
Assess strong authentication and authorisation for agent-initiated payments
Design dispute, refund and error-handling processes for agent transactions
syllabus: Agent-initiated payments, tokens and programmable money
Authentication, consent and transaction limits
Unauthorised, mistaken and disputed agent transactions
Settlement, reconciliation and stablecoin rails

modules.title: Controls, Monitoring and Kill-Switches
modules.summary: The control environment for agents that act: pre-deployment testing, guardrails, real-time monitoring, human intervention and the ability to stop an agent quickly.
objectives: Design layered controls and guardrails for agentic systems
Specify monitoring, logging and alerting for agent behaviour
Implement and test kill-switches and human override
syllabus: Testing, red-teaming and staged deployment
Guardrails, hard limits and tool restrictions
Real-time monitoring, audit trails and anomaly detection
Kill-switches, rollback and incident response

modules.title: Liability, Conduct and Customer Outcomes
modules.summary: Who is responsible when an agent gets it wrong, how conduct and consumer protection rules apply to agent actions, and how firms secure good customer outcomes.
objectives: Analyse liability allocation between the firm, customer and technology provider
Apply suitability, fair treatment and disclosure obligations to agent actions
Identify risks of manipulation, herding and harm to vulnerable customers
syllabus: Liability for errors, unauthorised acts and agent failures
Suitability, best interests and the advice boundary
Dark patterns, agent-to-agent manipulation and collusion
Vulnerable customers and outcome monitoring

modules.title: Financial Crime and Third-Party Model Risk
modules.summary: How agents can be exploited for fraud, money laundering and sanctions evasion, and how firms manage dependence on third-party models and agent platforms.
objectives: Recognise financial crime typologies involving AI agents
Adapt transaction monitoring and fraud controls to agent activity
Assess due diligence, concentration and exit risk for third-party models
syllabus: Agent-enabled fraud, account takeover and synthetic identities
Laundering and sanctions evasion through automated transactions
Third-party models, agent platforms and concentration risk
Contracts, audit rights and exit planning

modules.title: Governance, Board Oversight and Readiness
modules.summary: Brings the programme together into a governance framework and readiness plan, covering accountability, board oversight, supervisory engagement and international standards.
objectives: Define accountability for agentic AI under senior manager accountability regimes
Specify the information and assurance the board needs on agents
Produce an agentic AI readiness plan for the firm
syllabus: Accountability, risk appetite and approval of agent use cases
Board reporting, assurance and supervisory engagement
International work by the FSB, IOSCO, BIS and OECD
Workshop: the firm's agentic AI readiness plan

related.title: AI Governance for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving compliance, risk, model risk and technology staff the tools to design, run and evidence robust AI governance across the firm.

related.title: FinTech Business Models: Understanding and Supervising Innovation
related.summary: A ten-module programme equipping supervisors and firm compliance teams to understand how FinTech business models make money, grow and fail, and to assess their risks.

related.title: Digital Money and Tokenisation for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping banks, payment firms, asset managers and infrastructures decide whether and how to participate in digital money and tokenisation.

related.title: Operational Resilience and Cyber Risk for Firms
related.summary: A ten-module programme giving firms the tools to identify, map, test and evidence operational resilience and manage ICT, cyber and third-party risk.

related.title: Quantum and Cryptographic Resilience for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping firms understand the quantum threat, build a cryptographic inventory, plan post-quantum migration and report readiness to the board and supervisors.

related.title: Sustainable Finance and ESG for Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving firms the tools to manage climate and ESG risks, prepare credible disclosures and transition plans, and avoid greenwashing.
